text:
The Tkachuk brothers are on the same line in Florida, and this week they were the loudest story in hockey. Brady, traded from Ottawa to the Panthers, faced the Senators with Matthew on Wednesday, and the night produced a Matthew hit on Ottawa's Tyler Kleven that Player Safety chose not to punish and a hot-mic chirp that made the rounds. Sportsnet asked whether Matthew should have been fined. Whatever you think of it, the Panthers are 15-7-3 with three straight wins.

The same night brought better news: Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand returned, Marchand with three assists, and the Panthers called Barkov's emotional return "special" in their own video. Getting the captain back changes what this lineup can be.

Our numbers see a good team, not yet a dominant one. Florida gets 52% of the expected goals, and the goals at both ends sit close to what the chances say. The Tkachuk line with Sam Bennett has 58% of the expected goals but has only broken even on the scoreboard (11-10). Bennett, who scored Friday's winner in Washington after a hand-pass review, has 11 points in his last 10 on 6.5 expected, and Sandis Vilmanis has 8 on 3.4. Both will cool. Florida also lives on the edges, taking and drawing more than five penalties a game.

Our numbers give the Panthers a 78% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: where Paul Maurice slots Barkov, and what that does to a top six that is suddenly crowded.
